graphFamiliesNote: Case IDs identify resize transformations of Wien or Sydney. The source graphs alternate; methods and highlighting styles are randomized within that constraint.

part1.title: Part 1 · Match nodes in static drawings
part1.instruction: The four highlighted nodes on the left form a path. Select the same four nodes in the drawing on the right, shown at a different aspect ratio.
part1.targetsNote: Four consecutive vertices within attached trees, selected deterministically from original topology. The same target path is used for both methods.

part2.title: Part 2 · Track nodes through an animation
part2.instruction: Memorize the four red nodes along a path. Watch the graph change between square, very tall or very wide drawings. Blue nodes provide either structural or movement-based visual aids; these styles are mixed throughout this part. After playback, select the same four target nodes in the unmarked final drawing.

structural.label: Structural landmarks
structural.intro: Blue nodes mark structural landmarks: highly connected nodes and tree attachment nodes. Remember the four red target nodes before playback; the blue nodes are visual aids and may be different.

movement.label: Movement-based highlights
movement.intro: Blue nodes mark nodes or attached structures with large movement beyond the overall resize. Remember the four red target nodes before playback; the blue nodes are visual aids and may be different.

part3.title: Compare two animations
part3.instruction: Watch both animations of the same graph, then rate which animation you prefer. You can watch the pair as many times as you like.

questions.text: Which animation do you prefer overall?
